chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever eats food, let him mention the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over it. So if he forgets and remembers Allah afterwards, the Satan (may Allah curse him) vomits what he had eaten with him, and the man finds the food to be little.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to Satan when a person forgets to say Bismillah before eating and remembers later?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from Imam Ali (AS), establishes the spiritual mechanics of consumption, linking the physical act of eating to the metaphysical influence of Satan. It highlights a unique Shia scholarly perspective where forgetting the initial invocation is rectified by a subsequent remembrance, causing Satan to vomit the portion of food he 'consumed' with the believer, thereby reducing satiety as a sign of his diminished share. This serves as both a practical reminder for mindfulness and a theological explanation for varying degrees of fullness.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who eats food, so let him mention the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic over it. So if he were to forget, so he should mentioned Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from afterwards, the Satan<sup>la</sup>, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse him<sup>la</sup> vomits what he<sup>la</sup> had eaten (in participation) with him, and the man would find the meal as little’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘

One who eats food must mention the name of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious on it; but if one forgets and remembers later, Satan, may Allah condemn him, throws up what he has eaten and one feels as if the food is not sufficient.’”
